plateau

/pla-TOH/ — rhymes with go · noun

Hear It

What It Means

A plateau is a flat, raised area of land that sits higher than the ground surrounding it.

The village sits on a plateau, flat as a table above the winding river.

Worked Example

After climbing for hours, the hikers reached a plateau where they could rest on flat ground before continuing upward.

Plateau captures something specific: a raised flat area, combining both the elevation (higher than surroundings) and the flatness (unlike a mountain peak). 'Flat land' would miss the crucial sense of being raised up—the elevation is essential to what plateau means.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

tableland: A tableland is broad, flat country raised above everything around it — land shaped like a tabletop. It means nearly the same thing as plateau, but tableland is the loose, descriptive picture-word, while plateau is the precise geographic term you would find on a map or in a textbook.

terrace: A terrace is a single flat step cut or built into a slope, often one of a series — think of rice terraces stacked up a hillside. A plateau is far larger and stands on its own: one broad, flat expanse lifted above the surrounding land, not a step in a staircase.

shelf: A shelf is a narrow, flat ledge of land or rock jutting out partway up a larger slope, like a resting spot on the side of a cliff. A plateau is not a ledge on something else's side — it is its own broad, raised landform, flat across the top.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

valley: low land between hills or mountains

lowland: flat land lying at low elevation

Where it sits · how dramatically the flat ground is lifted — plain → highland → plateau → mesa

plain vs. plateau: A plain is flat land at any level, but a plateau is flat land lifted above everything around it.

highland vs. plateau: Highland describes any high country, hilly or rough, while a plateau is specifically a flat-topped raised area.

mesa vs. plateau: A mesa is an even more dramatic, steep-sided table of rock than a plateau, which can be broader and gentler at its edges.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — plateau

Root — plateau: a flat thing (French)

Put it together

Put it together: Plateau came into English as one whole French word: plateau, 'a flat thing,' built in French from plat ('flat') and an old noun ending, -eau, that had already fossilized in place. A plateau is literally that - a flat stretch of land raised above its surroundings. English never added a prefix or suffix; the word arrived whole and stayed whole.

Use the root in a new word: platter

Use the root in a new word: platter: He carried a platter of sandwiches, flat and wide enough to serve the whole team.

Word Choice

neutral

Plateau is the word for an elevated flat area—it's the geographical term. Use it for landscapes and in discussion of landforms. In everyday speech, you might say 'high, flat land' or use 'highland' if being less technical.
